# DR-0044 — sv2ms faces are generated by signature class

## Decision

The System V faces over the DLL's Microsoft-ABI bodies (WP-27) are not one
generic thunk and not sixteen hundred hand-written wrappers. They are
generated in four classes, decided per export by the shape of its C
prototype, and the classification is itself a generated, certified artifact:
`runtime/face/sigclass.tsv`, derived by `derive-sigclass.sh` from the host's
own headers through `gcc -aux-info`, total over the sv2ms rows of the face
table and pinned at int 1122, fp 307, aggr 10, unlisted 222.

The classes and their faces:

- **int** — every parameter and the result travel in the integer register
  file (integers, pointers, enums). The two conventions disagree only about
  which integer registers and stack slots carry which position, and that
  disagreement is uniform across arities: a face that forwards six integer
  arguments covers every function of six or fewer, because forwarding a
  register the callee never reads is harmless in both conventions — the
  caller owns the argument area, the callee reads only what its prototype
  names. So the int faces are generated from one shape without knowing any
  function's true arity.
- **fp** — a float, double, or long double anywhere in the signature. Here
  position maps to different register files in the two conventions (System V
  assigns integer and vector registers independently; Microsoft assigns by
  absolute position), so the face must be compiled from the true prototype,
  which the classification records in its third column for exactly this use.
- **aggr** — a by-value struct or union parameter or result. The conventions
  disagree about when an aggregate rides in registers versus behind a hidden
  pointer, so these ten faces are also compiled from their recorded
  prototypes.
- **unlisted** — no public header declares the name (Cygwin-internal
  entry points, `__`-prefixed helpers, the fortify `_chk` family). The face
  generator's disposition for these is decided when it is built, from
  Cygwin's own declarations rather than guesses; this record only fixes that
  they are a named class the total count keeps visible, not a remainder that
  silently falls into a default.

## Why the prototypes come from `gcc -aux-info`

The signature lives in exactly one place, the C prototype, and the reliable
reader of C prototypes is a C compiler. `-aux-info` makes the host gcc emit
every declaration it saw in canonical one-line form after preprocessing,
which handles the multi-line declarations, macros, and conditional
compilation that defeated the text scan `derive-variadic.sh` already
documents as an aid rather than a source. The probe TU names the header
surface breadth-first; a name it cannot reach is classified unlisted rather
than guessed at.

## What this forecloses

A single arity-blind generic face for the whole surface. The 307 fp and 10
aggr rows are the measured refutation: `ldexp (double, int)` places its
integer in `%rdi` under System V and in `%rdx` under Microsoft, and no
register move that ignores the signature gets both `ldexp` and `accept`
right. The count is also the guard: `t/sigclass.sh` pins the class totals,
so a header drift that silently moves part of the surface between classes
fails a test rather than changing which generator shape a face gets.

## Revisit

If the face generator finds an unlisted export whose true signature is not
integer-class, the generic shape cannot carry it; the resolution is a
recorded prototype in the generator's own table, and this record gains the
list of such exceptions.
